title: In vitro infection of primary chicken lymphocytes with Marek's disease virus
protocol: Propagate CEC monolayers to a confluency of 80–90%.
Trypsinize cells and mix 1–2 × 10^6 of the CEC with MDV-infected CEC (3 × 10^4 plaque-forming units [pfu]) per 6-well plate (∼9.6 m²).
Seed cell mixture in 6-wells.
Incubate at 37°C under a 5% CO2 atmosphere for 3–4 days.
Infect larger cell culture dishes with 3 × 10^4 pfu for 3–4 days until the culture is completely infected.
Trypsinize the cells and use them to infect fresh or passaged CEC at a 1-to-5 ratio for another 2–3 days until almost all cells are infected.
Freeze infected CEC stocks using DMSO as cryoprotective agent following standard protocols.
Homogenize the bursa/thymus through a 40 μm cell strainer to obtain a uniform single-cell suspension.
Leave cell suspension at room temperature for 10 min.
Apply the supernatant onto a lymphocyte separating solution and spin for 12 minutes at 650 × g with slow acceleration and deactivated deceleration.
Carefully transfer lymphocytes at the interphase into a new tube.
Wash lymphocytes with PBS.
Maintain cells in growth medium at 41°C and 5% CO2.
Activate cells using recombinant soluble chicken CD40L for B-cells and anti-chicken TCR alpha/beta antibody for T-cells.
Grow suspension cell cultures of chicken B- or T-cell lines if needed.
Microscopically monitor virus replication for 3-4 days until the whole monolayer is infected.
Seed 1 × 10^6 to 1 × 10^7 lymphocytes per well onto the infected CEC.
Incubate at 41°C and 5% CO2 for 16 hours.
Gently sway the cell culture dish 1-2 hours post seeding of the lymphocytes.
Carefully remove suspension cells with the cell culture supernatant.
Pellet them at 250 × g for 5 minutes.
Optionally, use a PBS wash to collect lymphocytes remaining on the CEC monolayer after the first harvest of the suspension cells.
Resuspend the pellet in growth medium and culture the resuspended cells at 41°C and 5% CO2 overnight.
Alternatively, directly FACS-sort the cells to obtain a pure infected lymphocyte population.
Thaw the frozen cryovial with infected CEC in a water bath at 37°C.
Transfer the content of the cryovial into a 50 mL falcon tube.
Add PBS or medium without FBS drop by drop while continuously shaking the tube.
Fill the tube up to 50 mL with PBS or medium.
Centrifuge the mixture at 250 × g for 10 minutes at room temperature.
Carefully remove the supernatant.
Resuspend the infected cell pellet in 5 mL of lymphocyte suspension (1 × 10^7 cells per mL).
Plate CEC/lymphocyte mix in wells of a 24-well plate, using 1 mL of the suspension per well.
Incubate the cells at 41°C and 5% CO2 for 16–24 hours.
Proceed with FACS or any other downstream analysis.
